q: A hot sunny morning, calm. By 14:00 a steady 15-knot onshore wind has set in. What is it?
answer: A sea breeze — it will die at sunset
why: Warm land draws air in from the sea on sunny afternoons.

q: Wind is forecast to go round to the south overnight. Which spot do you anchor in?
answer: Spot A — sheltered by the land to the south
why: Choose shelter from the forecast wind, not the present one.

figure.note: Forecast: wind backing south overnight, F5

ru.Forecast: wind backing south overnight,: Прогноз: ночью ветер отходит к Ю, 5 баллов

q: The wind is pinning you against the pontoon. How do you leave?
answer: Spring the stern out: bow spring led aft, fender the bow, helm towards the pontoon, gently ahead, then astern clear
why: Ahead against a bow spring pivots the boat on the bow and swings the stern out into the wind.

q: You are sailing along this coast towards the next harbour. What is it called, and how far off do you keep?
answer: A lee shore; keep well off
why: A lee shore has the wind blowing onto it; a failure there drives you onto the rocks.

q: A crew member wants to swim from the yacht to the beach. What do you insist on?
answer: A bright tow float, clear of the tender route
why: A swimmer's head is almost invisible to a rib driver; a bright float and a clear route save lives.

figure.note: Y: your yacht, 300 m off the beach

ru.Y: your yacht, 300 m off the beach: Y: ваша яхта, в 300 м от пляжа

q: You plan to pass through the strait at A. What do you expect?
answer: F7 or more and steep seas — consider waiting
why: Wind funnels and accelerates between high islands; the Kafireas Strait is notorious.

q: Menorca, July. Tramontana F6 is forecast for tonight. Where do you spend the night?
answer: B, on the south coast
why: The Tramontana is a northerly: shelter on the south side of the island.

q: You are anchored off a hot island in summer. Yesterday afternoon the wind blew onshore. What is this light breeze?
answer: A land breeze — it fades after sunrise
why: At night the land cools below the sea and air drains offshore; it dies as the sun heats the land.

figure.note: 05:00 after a clear night, wind off the land

ru.05:00 after a clear night, wind off the: 05:00 после ясной ночи, ветер с берега

q: You are anchored at A. At 02:00 strong cold gusts pour down off the land. What is it, and what do you do next time?
answer: Katabatic — avoid the valley mouth
why: On clear nights cold air drains down valleys and bursts out of their mouths.

q: Same F6 wind across the whole gulf. Where is the sea smallest?
answer: A — near the windward shore, short fetch
why: Waves grow with the distance the wind blows over open water (the fetch).

q: Where will you spend a comfortable night?
answer: B — tucked away from the swell
why: Swell can make an anchorage untenable even in light wind; hide from the swell direction.

q: You must pick a night anchorage. Which one?
answer: B — sheltered now and after the shift
why: Choose shelter for the wind you will have overnight, not only the wind you have now.

figure.note: Now NW 5 · backing SW 6 after midnight

ru.Now NW 5 · backing SW 6 after midnight: Сейчас СЗ 5 · после полуночи отходит на ЮЗ 6

q: Looking down through clear water you see this bottom. Where do you drop the anchor?
answer: B — on the sand, clear of the seagrass
why: Posidonia seagrass is protected and holds poorly; anchor and chain belong on sand.

figure.note: Seen from the bow, depth about 6 m

ru.Seen from the bow, depth about 6 m: Вид с носа, глубина около 6 м

q: Which spot gives you the quietest night?
answer: A — tucked in behind the headland
why: Swell, not just wind, decides comfort; anchor behind land that blocks it.

figure.note: Wind NW F3 · old swell rolling in from the SW

ru.Wind NW F3 · old swell rolling in from t: Ветер СЗ, 3 балла · старая зыбь заходит с ЮЗ

q: You are anchored here for the night. What do you do?
answer: Leave before dark for a bay sheltered from the west
why: A bay open to the forecast wind becomes a lee shore; move while it is light.

figure.note: Forecast: wind W F6 after midnight

ru.Forecast: wind W F6 after midnight: Прогноз: после полуночи ветер З, 6 баллов

q: You arrive in this bay. Where do you let go your anchor?
answer: C — well to one side, clear of its swing
why: Never drop over another boat's chain; keep both swinging circles apart.

labels: yacht at anchor, 40 m chain out

q: You are motoring towards spot A to anchor. How do you make the final approach?
answer: Slowly, head to wind, stopping over the spot
why: Head to wind you can stop exactly where you want and fall back in line.

q: You will moor stern-to in the marked berth. Where do you drop the anchor?
answer: B — upwind of the line of the berth
why: Dropped upwind, the chain holds the bow up to windward as you reverse.

figure.note: Wind on the beam of the berth, F4

q: From which spot do you start your final approach to the buoy?
answer: A — so you motor slowly up into the wind
why: Approach a buoy into the wind so you can stop beside it.

q: You are alongside and an offshore breeze holds the bow away from the pontoon. Which line pulls it in close?
answer: A bow breast line, square to the pontoon
why: Breast lines run at right angles and pull the boat in; springs stop surge.

q: You come alongside this pontoon. How do you approach?
answer: At a steeper angle, getting a line on fast
why: Wind off the berth blows you away; aim in more and get a line ashore quickly.

q: This time the wind blows onto the berth. How do you come alongside?
answer: Stop parallel, a metre off; let the wind push you in
why: An onshore wind does the work; arrive stopped and parallel, well fendered.

q: You will swing the stern out and leave astern. What do you rig, and which gear?
answer: Bow spring led aft, bow fendered, gently ahead
why: Ahead against a bow spring pivots on the bow and swings the stern out.
